identity.title: POCUS IVC: diameter and respiratory collapsibility (subxiphoid long axis, 2-3 cm from RA junction)

technique.how: Supine patient; phased-array or curvilinear probe subxiphoid, sagittal, following the IVC into the right atrium. Measure maximal and minimal diameter 2-3 cm caudal to the RA junction (just distal to the hepatic vein) over a respiratory cycle, in B-mode or M-mode. Collapsibility index = (max-min)/max in spontaneous breathing; distensibility index in mechanically ventilated patients.
technique.prerequisites: Confirm the vessel is the IVC (enters RA, hepatic vein inflow) not the aorta; standardized breathing.

interpretation.positive_finding: Small IVC (<2.1 cm) collapsing >50% suggests low right atrial pressure and, in shock, possible fluid responsiveness (pooled sensitivity 0.63-0.71, specificity 0.73-0.75).
interpretation.negative_finding: A dilated, non-collapsing IVC (>2.1 cm, <50% collapse) indicates elevated RA pressure (RV failure, tamponade, volume overload, tension pneumothorax) and argues against further fluid; it does not exclude fluid responsiveness.
interpretation.pitfalls: Measurement is unreliable with irregular breathing, abdominal pressure, mechanical ventilation at low tidal volumes, athletes, and when the sample is taken at the wrong level or off-axis (cylinder effect). It predicts fluid responsiveness only modestly and worst in spontaneously breathing patients.
interpretation.changes_what: Plethoric IVC: stop empiric fluids and look at RV, pericardium and lungs. Collapsing IVC in shock: give fluid bolus and reassess. Intermediate: use dynamic tests instead.

estimates.target_condition: Fluid responsiveness (positive IVC respiratory variation, study-specific thresholds)
estimates.population: 533 patients with acute circulatory failure, all ages, spontaneously and mechanically ventilated; 17 prospective studies; 253 (47%) responders
estimates.reference_standard: Increase in stroke volume/cardiac output after fluid challenge (recognized reference standard per study)
estimates.quote: predictor of fluid responsiveness were 0.63 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.56-0.69) and 0.73 (95% CI: 0.67-0.78), respectively

estimates.target_condition: Fluid responsiveness (caval index: IVC collapsibility or distensibility)
estimates.population: Critically ill adults and children, ventilated or not; 20 studies in meta-analysis (26 caval-index studies included)
estimates.reference_standard: Increase in cardiac output after fluid challenge or passive leg raise (study-specific)

sources.citation: Long E, Oakley E, Duke T, Babl FE. Does Respiratory Variation in Inferior Vena Cava Diameter Predict Fluid Responsiveness: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Shock. 2017;47(5):550-559.

Orso D, Paoli I, Piani T, Cilenti FL, Cristiani L, Guglielmo N. Accuracy of Ultrasonographic Measurements of Inferior Vena Cava to Determine Fluid Responsiveness: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Intensive Care Med. 2020;35(4):354-363.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use IVC collapsibility as the sole guide to fluids in spontaneously breathing patients, in raised intra-abdominal pressure, or on ventilator settings outside those studied; a negative test cannot rule out fluid responsiveness.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Plethoric IVC with hypotension: evaluate immediately for tamponade, RV failure/massive PE or tension pneumothorax rather than giving fluid.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Both meta-analyses note extreme heterogeneity in thresholds (12-50% variation), measurement site and ventilation mode; Long 2017 subgroup shows better performance in mechanically ventilated patients.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Operator can obtain a true long-axis subxiphoid IVC view, distinguish IVC from aorta, and measure at a fixed distance from the RA junction with M-mode; understands ventilation-mode dependence.

extraction_notes: Both pooled estimates are quoted from abstracts (Shock and J Intensive Care Med are not PMC OA). Orso quote lists AUC 0.71, log DOR 2.02, then sensitivity 0.71 and specificity 0.75 in order; values assigned per abstract sentence order. The estimates address fluid responsiveness, not RA-pressure estimation; the ASE 2010/2015 IVC-based RAP cut-offs (2.1 cm, 50%) used in interpretation are guideline consensus and were not fetched/cited numerically within budget.
